preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and k >= 1 and k <= n
preconditions.description: The number of nodes n is at least 2, and k is a positive integer not exceeding n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= 1_000_000 for a_i in a)
preconditions.description: Each a_i (time spent on the i-th ball) is an integer between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n and u_i != v_i for u_i, v_i in edges)
preconditions.description: The input contains exactly n-1 edges, each connecting two distinct nodes in the range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: all(u_i != v_j or (u_i == v_j and v_i == u_j) for i in range(len(edges)) for j in range(len(edges)) if i != j)
preconditions.description: The edges form a valid tree (no cycles, no duplicate edges).

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum possible grade Jacob can achieve, which is between 1 and 1,000,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == max(min(a[dfs_order[:k]] for dfs_order in possible_dfs_orders(a, edges)) for root in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum value of the minimum a_i in the first k nodes of any DFS traversal, where the traversal is rooted at any node and the neighbor order is optimally chosen to maximize this minimum.
